comments.content: `h.container` is the single app-wide `*container.Container` injected into every registered route (see `gofr.go:106` and `rest.go:45`), and `container.Logger` is a plain interface field with no synchronization. Writing to it here means every concurrent request mutates the same field: overlapping requests race, and one request's deferred restore (`h.container.Logger = origLogger`) can permanently install another request's `ContextLogger` as the global logger. That both leaks a finished request's trace ID into unrelated logs and can reset the logger to a stale wrapper. The request-scoped logger should not be stored on the shared container; thread it through the request context/handler instead, or make the logger resolve the trace ID per call from the goroutine's context.

comments.content: Using a magic `map[string]any{"__trace_id__": ...}` sentinel conflates user data with internal metadata. Any caller that logs a `map[string]any` containing a string `"__trace_id__"` key will have that entry silently stripped from the message (and the whole map dropped), and the handling is inconsistent: only the first such map is consumed, while subsequent maps with the same key are re-appended and printed as message content. Consider a dedicated unexported wrapper type for trace metadata instead of a key users can collide with.

comments.content: The trace-ID injection relies on the wrapped logger silently stripping the `__trace_id__` map, but only the package-internal `*logger.logf` does that (`extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs`). `ContextLogger` is exported and `NewContextLogger` accepts any `logging.Logger`, so wrapping an implementation that does not know about the sentinel breaks its output. Concretely, `logging.NewMockLogger` (used by `container.NewMockContainer`, and available to users for tests) forwards straight to `fmt.Sprintf`, so `MockLogger.Infof("%s", "x")` wrapped by `ContextLogger` prints `x%!(EXTRA map[string]interface {}{__trace_id__:...})` and leaks internal metadata into the log line. Same for any user-supplied custom logger assigned to the container. The contract should be explicit: handle the sentinel in every implementation (at least `MockLogger.logf`), or annotate the trace ID through a dedicated interface that `ContextLogger` can type-assert and degrade gracefully when absent.

func extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs(args []any) (traceID string, filtered []any) {
	filtered = make([]any, 0, len(args))
